title: The "I Before E" Rule & Exception Patterns

Memorize key high-frequency exceptions (friend, science, height)

💡 Solution: Mnemonic: C + EI = Ceiling, Receive, Receipt!

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: The "I Before E" Rule & Exception Patterns
1. Definition: Spelling rule predicting whether to write IE or EI for the long /iː/ sound.
2. Rule: « I before E, except after C, or when sounding like A, as in neighbor and weigh. »
3. Why? Anglo-Norman French spelling conventions influenced English orthography.
4. How to recognize? Long /iː/ sound spelled with i and e.
5. Common examples: believe /bɪˈliːv/, relief, field, piece vs receive /rɪˈsiːv/, ceiling, receipt vs neighbor /ˈneɪbər/, weigh /weɪ/
6. Counter-examples: friend /frɛnd/ (short e sound); science /ˈsaɪəns/ (two syllables).
7. Exceptions: height /haɪt/, weird /wɪərd/, foreign /ˈfɔːrən/, seize /siːz/, protein /ˈproʊtiːn/.
8. Common mistakes: Writing *recieve instead of receive after C.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: I before E except after C! Receive has C, so E comes first!
10. Key vocabulary: I before E, spelling rule, long e sound, French borrowing, exceptions
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🟡 A2
13. Associated Visual: 🔤 Rhyme card: I before E except after C!
14. Key Takeaway: I before E! After C = EI! Sounding like A = EI!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: In 'believe', why is it IE? (Because it does not follow the letter C)
CCQ 2: In 'receive', why is it EI? (Because it comes after C)
CCQ 3: How is EI pronounced in 'neighbor' and 'weigh'? (/eI/ long a sound)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Complete with IE or EI:
🎯 Item: bel_ _ve ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: believe (IE)
🎯 Item: rec_ _ve ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: receive (EI after C)
🎯 Item: w_ _gh ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: weigh (EI = /eɪ/)
